subject: Post-bakeoff synthesis — prioritized experiments & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@hearthcare.com>, Luke Harrow <lukeh@hearthcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-bakeoff synthesis — prioritized experiments & next steps

Hi Marta / Luke —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick synthesis from our side so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. TL;DR: there are three priority experiments we recommend running in your sandbox this week to validate performance and cost claims from the other vendors. I attached a short bakeoff matrix and a smoke-test checklist.

Key pain points you raised
- P1: Latency spikes under peak—p50 target <= 200ms for short-chat flows, worst-case tail < 800ms.
- P2: Cost predictability — current model ops pipeline makes unit costs volatile at scale.
- P3: Model fidelity/consistency — hallucination risk when population prompts shift; you want stable few-shot outputs.
- P4: Data residency + auditability for PHI-sensitive flows.

Goals we heard
- 6-week pilot to prove latency & cost targets for a 3k concurrent-session workload.
- Clear fallbacks for degraded model variants and automated routing in region.
- Procurement-signed commercial terms and an SSO/SAML onboarding window in July.

Competitive notes (what we saw today)
- VendorX: superior raw throughput in batch, but missing prefix/KV caching and structured fallback routing.
- VendorY: aggressive price quotes that rely on aggressive quantization (some quality tradeoffs we flagged).
- Redwood: unified routing, auto-prefix/KV cache, and tailored quantization profiles — gives predictable p50 latency with configurable cost SLOs.

Recommended priority experiments (short, runnable in your sandbox)
1) Realistic load run (owner: Rishi) — 3k concurrent sessions, production prompt distribution, compare p50/p95 across variants.
2) Prefix/KV caching smoke (owner: Camila) — replay your common dialogs to measure token-cost reduction and tail latency improvement.
3) QoS vs quantization (owner: Marissa) — run fidelity checks on representative prompts with our 4-bit profile vs competitor profile.

Immediate asks / next steps
- I: Share the bakeoff-priority-matrix.xlsx and smoke-test-plan.md (attached).
- II: Rishi will request temporary sandbox creds and a small test dataset (non-PHI) to run the experiments.
- III: Marissa to follow up with a draft pilot commercial summary for procurement (SOW + price bands).
- IV: Can you confirm procurement contact and your legal review timeline?

Attached: bakeoff-priority-matrix.xlsx, smoke-test-plan.md

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the tests.

—
Camila Reyes

Camila — thanks for the thorough recap. This format is great and aligns with what I want to present internally. A couple of notes from procurement / engineering: 

- Procurement asked if you can provide a short SOW template + high-level pilot pricing (not a formal quote yet) — they want to see commitment length, termination & data handling language up front.
- Engineering: can you confirm if the sandbox credentials will be ephemeral and whether there is an IP allowlist option? We cannot use PHI in tests; we'll provide sanitized dataset.
- Competitor note: VendorY told us they can meet our cost target by using a 3-bit proprietary quant — curious how Redwood's 4-bit profile compares on fidelity checks.

We should get you a list of procurement reviewers early next week. Looping procurement in now so they can track.

Thanks,
Marta

Camila / Rishi — quick internal note to capture what I think we should own for the next 10 days: 
- Marissa: commercial pilot summary + procurement touchpoint (SOW draft, price bands, SLA bullets).
- Camila: lead on prefix/KV caching smoke and coordinate sandbox creds.
- Rishi: run load experiments and produce the p50/p95 report (include competitor baseline).

Timeline proposal:
- Mon/Tue: get sandbox access + sanitized dataset from HearthCare.
- Wed/Thu: run smoke tests + caching replay.
- Fri: consolidate findings and deliver a short readout + suggested canary week (week of Jun 14).

One more ask — we should include a quick decision rubric in the readout: latency, cost per 1M tokens, fidelity regression (A/B), and ops overhead (integration effort). I'll draft a one-pager and drop it in the drive link.

-Marissa

Hi Marta / Luke / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick reply and the procurement heads-up. Short answers and attachments below.

1) Sandbox creds — we will provision ephemeral keys on an allowlist. Rishi will send a request form; keys will expire after 14 days by default. No PHI should be uploaded; thanks for the sanitized dataset.

2) SOW + pilot pricing — attached is a one-page pilot SOW and a pilot pricing band (SLA-summary.pdf). This is a starter doc for procurement; happy to iterate.

3) Quantization & fidelity — our recommended 4-bit profile preserves few-shot fidelity for the prompt classes you shared in the call; we included a short fidelity checklist in smoke-test-plan.md. We'll run that head-to-head against VendorY's profile in the same experiment run.

4) Proposed canary week — Jun 14–18 (tentative). If that works, Marissa will draft the prep checklist for your ops team.

Action items (owners)
- Rishi (redwood): request sandbox access form to HearthCare and provision ephemeral creds.
- Marissa (redwood): SOW draft + pricing bands to procurement (attached).
